story: An online seller took Rs 8,000 for a phone on 15 October 2026 and never delivered. Can I file a case under IPC 420 against them? I am in Kolkata.

timeline.event: Paid Rs 8,000 to an online seller for a phone
timeline.user_words: An online seller took Rs 8,000 for a phone on 15 October 2026 and never delivered

facts.user_goal: File a case under IPC 420 against the seller

rules.name: consumer_limitation
rules.message: File your consumer complaint before 15 Oct 2028 (707 days left). This counts 2 years from 15 Oct 2026 (your purchase date - counted from the earliest possible day, to be safe). Don't wait for the last date. Sending a letter or calling the helpline does NOT pause this clock.

facts_used.start_basis: purchase date (earliest possible start, to be safe)

rules.label: Last date to file your consumer complaint

rules.name: forum_and_fee
rules.message: You paid Rs 8,000, so the complaint goes to the District Consumer Commission, with no filing fee. You can file in the district where you live or work, online at e-jagriti.gov.in. You don't need a lawyer to file.
rules.label: Where to file

rules.name: free_first_steps
rules.message: Two free steps often work first: (1) a written complaint to the seller's or platform's grievance officer, (2) the National Consumer Helpline: call 1915 or WhatsApp 8800001915.
rules.label: Try these first

answer.summary: You can file a consumer complaint for your undelivered phone. You have over two years left to do so, and the filing fee is zero. You do not need to file under IPC 420, which is for criminal cheating and was replaced by BNS s.318(4). You can file online at e-jagriti.gov.in.

claims.text: You can file a consumer complaint because you are a consumer who bought goods for personal use, not for business.
The seller's failure to deliver the phone is an unfair trade practice, as they took your money but did not provide the goods.
You can file your complaint with the District Consumer Commission, and there is no filing fee because the amount is up to Rs 5 lakh.
You can file the complaint online at e-jagriti.gov.in.
You have until 15 October 2028 to file your consumer complaint.

next_steps.action: Call the National Consumer Helpline at 1915 or WhatsApp 8800001915 to register your complaint.
next_steps.why: This is a free first step that can help you recover your money without going to court.

next_steps.action: Send a written complaint to the seller's or the online platform's grievance officer asking for a refund.
next_steps.why: This is a free step that creates a record of your demand for a refund.

next_steps.action: File your complaint online at e-jagriti.gov.in.
next_steps.why: You do not need a lawyer. You can file from your home in Kolkata.

next_steps.action: Gather your proof of payment and any tracking or delivery details you have.
next_steps.why: You need these to support your complaint.

questions_for_user: Do you have any proof of payment, such as a bank statement, screenshot, or receipt?
Do you have a tracking number or any email or chat history with the seller?

support.text: You can file a consumer complaint because you are a consumer who bought goods for personal use, not for business.
support.reason: The law text defines 'consumer' as a person who buys goods for consideration (paid/promised/partly paid/promised, or deferred payment) and explicitly excludes a person who obtains goods for resale or commercial purpose. The sentence states the person bought goods for personal use, not business, which aligns with the law text's definition and exclusion.

support.text: The seller's failure to deliver the phone is an unfair trade practice, as they took your money but did not provide the goods.
support.reason: The law text states that refusing to take back defective goods or refund consideration within the stipulated period (or 30 days if no stipulation) is an unfair trade practice. The sentence describes the seller taking money but not providing goods, which constitutes a failure to deliver/refund, matching the unfair trade practice described in the law text.

support.text: You can file your complaint with the District Consumer Commission, and there is no filing fee because the amount is up to Rs 5 lakh.
support.reason: The law text states the District Commission has jurisdiction where the value does not exceed one crore rupees, with power for Central Government to prescribe other values. It does not mention any filing fee or amount up to Rs 5 lakh. The sentence adds a filing fee condition (no fee up to Rs 5 lakh) that is not in the law text.

support.text: You can file your complaint with the District Consumer Commission, and there is no filing fee because the amount is up to Rs 5 lakh.

support.text: You can file the complaint online at e-jagriti.gov.in.
support.reason: The law text states that complaints 'may be filed electronically in such manner as may be prescribed.' The sentence states the complaint can be filed online at e-jagriti.gov.in, which is an electronic method of filing, consistent with the law text's provision for electronic filing.

support.text: You have until 15 October 2028 to file your consumer complaint.
support.reason: The law text states complaints must be filed within two years from the date the cause of action arose, with discretion to condone delay for sufficient cause. The sentence specifies '15 October 2028' as the deadline, which adds a specific date not contained in the law text. The law text provides a general two-year period, not a specific calendar date.

draft_notes:
How to send it:
1. Find their correct address in the invoice, order page, or the seller's 'grievance officer' details on the website/app.
2. Fill every [FILL] slot. Remove anything that isn't true - only state facts you can prove.
3. Send by Speed Post and keep the receipt and the tracking proof of delivery. Also send a copy by email or WhatsApp and keep a screenshot.
4. Wait 15 days. Sending this letter does NOT stop any legal time limit - file your claim/complaint before the deadline shown, even if they haven't replied.
5. Free help to check the letter: legal aid 15100 or Tele-Law 14454.

Laws this letter relies on: Consumer Protection Act, 2019, s.69 (Two-year limitation and condonation); Consumer Protection Act, 2019, s.34(2) (Where to file: District Commission); Consumer Protection Act, 2019, s.35(1) (Who may file a complaint; e-filing)
